description: Is each Trickster process healthy as a Go program: restarts, configuration reloads, recovered panics, dropped log lines, and CPU, memory, GC and file-descriptor pressure.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Process restarts over the time range (changes of the process start time), summed across the selected instances. Only in-place restarts that keep the same instance address are seen; a replaced pod with a new address shows up as a new instance instead. Orange on any restart: check the logs for a crash, OOM kill or failed liveness probe.

panels.title: Config loaded OK
panels.description: OK when the most recent configuration apply (startup or reload) succeeded on every selected instance; FAILED when at least one instance's last reload failed or a startup step (geo ACL, log writer, tracing, routes, autodiscovery) failed. A failed reload is rolled back, so FAILED means the instance still serves its previous configuration. The timeline below shows which instance and when.

panels.title: Reload failures
panels.description: Configuration reloads that failed over the time range (the new config could not be loaded, validated or applied and was rolled back), summed across instances. Triggered by SIGHUP, the management reload endpoint, the config file auto-reloader or the Kubernetes controller. A later successful reload resets 'Config loaded OK' but not this count.

panels.title: Recovered panics
panels.description: Panics caught in background goroutines over the time range, across all six recovery points (proxy engines, cache index workers, ALB pool refresh, health probe loops, health status notifications and the health status page). The process survives, but each one is a bug; the table below names the component. The first panic of a new series is counted too.

targets.expr: (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0)) + (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: Logs dropped
panels.description: Access and error log lines dropped over the time range because the log writer could not keep up (shared buffer full) or its file could not be written, rather than blocking requests. A few around a reload are expected while the old writer closes. Requires an access_log to be configured; 0 otherwise.

targets.expr: (sum(((last_over_time(trickster_accesslog_dropped_lines_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_accesslog_dropped_lines_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_accesslog_dropped_lines_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) or vector(0))

panels.title: CPU / GOMAXPROCS
panels.description: CPU used by the busiest selected instance as a share of the cores the Go scheduler may use (GOMAXPROCS). Near 100% the process is CPU-bound: latency rises and garbage collection falls behind. On Linux, recent Go versions size GOMAXPROCS from the container's CPU limit.

targets.expr: (max(sum by (instance) (rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (instance) max by (instance) (go_sched_gomaxprocs_threads{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}))) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Mem / GOMEMLIMIT
panels.description: Memory the Go runtime holds (obtained from the OS minus what it has released) as a share of the soft memory limit GOMEMLIMIT, for the closest-to-limit instance. Near 100% the garbage collector runs back to back to stay under the limit, burning CPU. 'no limit' means GOMEMLIMIT is not set; memory caches live on this heap, so size them with the limit in mind.

targets.expr: (max((max by (instance) (go_memstats_sys_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (go_memstats_heap_released_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})) / on (instance) max by (instance) (go_gc_gomemlimit_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} < 1e18))) or vector(-1)

panels.title: FD utilization
panels.description: Open file descriptors (sockets, cache files, log files) of the fullest selected instance as a share of its limit. Near 100%, new connections fail to be accepted (EMFILE) and file-backed caches cannot open objects. n/a on platforms where the process collector cannot read descriptor counts.

targets.expr: (max(max by (instance) (process_open_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) / on (instance) (max by (instance) (process_max_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) > 0))) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Config load status by instance
panels.description: Per instance, whether its most recent configuration apply succeeded (OK, green) or failed (FAILED, red) over time. A failed reload rolls back, so a red stretch means that instance kept serving its previous configuration until the next successful reload; it was not down. Purple annotations mark successful reloads, orange ones restarts.

panels.title: Config age by instance
panels.description: Per instance, how long ago its configuration was last applied successfully, at startup or by a reload. Until the first reload this is about the process uptime. Instances whose ages differ a lot may be running different configurations.

panels.title: Reload attempts, successes and failures
panels.description: Configuration reloads per interval (at least one minute), summed across instances. Attempts count every reload request (SIGHUP, management endpoint, file auto-reloader, Kubernetes controller) before any check, so attempts skipped because the configuration had not changed, or because shutdown was in progress, appear only as attempts. Successes applied a new configuration; failures were rolled back. The initial load at startup is not a reload and is not counted.

panels.title: Reload duration (time range)
panels.description: Mean and 90th percentile wall time of the reloads in the time range that got past the 'unchanged' check, from start to success or failure. Successful reloads include waiting for the new listeners to become ready (bounded by twice reload_drain_timeout), so a long reload usually means a listener was slow to start. The histogram's buckets are 50 ms, 100 ms, 500 ms, 1 s, 5 s, 10 s and 20 s, so the p90 is a coarse interpolation; trust the mean.

targets.expr: (histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (increase(trickster_config_reload_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))) and on () (sum(increase(trickster_config_reload_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])) > 0)) or vector(-1)

panels.title: Recovered panics in time range
panels.description: Every recovery point that caught at least one panic in the time range, by instance. The detail column is the call site for proxy engine goroutines, the worker (flusher, reaper, scanner, refresh) for the cache index and ALB pool refresh, and the backend for health checks. Severity: a cache index panic leaves that worker stopped until the next reload or restart (stale index, no eviction); an ALB pool refresh panic keeps routing on the previous healthy member set until a later rebuild succeeds; the others skip one unit of work and carry on. Empty means no panics. Pair each row with the stack trace in the logs.

targets.expr:
(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance, site) (((last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "proxy engine goroutine", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "site", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance, worker) (((last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "cache index worker", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "worker", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance, worker) (((last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "ALB pool refresh", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "worker", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance, backend_name) (((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "health probe loop", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "backend_name", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (instance, backend_name) (((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "health status notify", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "backend_name", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(sum by (instance) (((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__range)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_handler_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "component", "health status page", "", "")) > 0

panels.title: Recovered panics by component
panels.description: When panics were recovered, per interval (at least one minute), by component and site, worker or backend (summed across instances), to line them up with deploys, reloads (purple annotations) or traffic changes. The first panic of a new series is included. Any bar is a bug.

targets.expr:
(label_replace(label_replace(sum by (site) (((last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__rate_interval)) or increase(trickster_proxy_engines_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), "component", "proxy engine goroutine", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "site", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (worker) (((last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__rate_interval)) or increase(trickster_cache_index_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), "component", "cache index worker", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "worker", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (worker) (((last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__rate_interval)) or increase(trickster_alb_pool_refresh_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), "component", "ALB pool refresh", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "worker", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (backend_name) (((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__rate_interval)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_probe_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), "component", "health probe loop", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "backend_name", "(.*)")
 or label_replace(label_replace(sum by (backend_name) (((last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m]) unless last_over_time(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[5m] offset $__rate_interval)) or increase(trickster_healthcheck_status_notify_panic_recovered_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval]))), "component", "health status notify", "", ""), "detail", "$1", "backend_name", "(.*)")

panels.title: Dropped log lines/s by backend and log
panels.description: Access and error log lines dropped per second, by the backend whose route wrote them ('-' is the router logger for requests that matched no route) and by log (access or error). Drops mean the log writer's shared buffer was full or its file could not be opened or rotated; requests are never blocked by logging. A short burst around a reload is expected; sustained drops mean the log destination is too slow for the request rate.

panels.title: Build, uptime and runtime settings by instance
panels.description: Per instance: the Trickster build (revision is empty for local builds), when the process started and its uptime, and the Go runtime settings that shape its performance: GOMAXPROCS (cores the scheduler uses), GOGC (heap growth percentage between collections) and GOMEMLIMIT (soft memory limit; '-' when unset).

targets.expr: max by (instance, version, revision, goversion) (trickster_build_info{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

panels.title: Saturation by instance
panels.description: Each instance's current CPU use against GOMAXPROCS, memory held from the OS against GOMEMLIMIT, and open file descriptors against the process limit. A gauge is missing when its limit is unset (no GOMEMLIMIT) or not exported (file descriptors outside Linux).

targets.expr: sum by (instance) (rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])) / on (instance) max by (instance) (go_sched_gomaxprocs_threads{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})

(max by (instance) (go_memstats_sys_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) - max by (instance) (go_memstats_heap_released_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"})) / on (instance) max by (instance) (go_gc_gomemlimit_bytes{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"} < 1e18)
max by (instance) (process_open_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) / on (instance) (max by (instance) (process_max_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) > 0)

panels.title: Goroutines and OS threads
panels.description: Live goroutines (solid) and OS threads (dashed) per instance. Trickster runs goroutines per connection, per in-flight origin fetch and per health probe, so goroutines track traffic; a steady climb while traffic is flat suggests a leak (for example upstreams that ignore cancellation). Threads rise with blocking syscalls such as disk cache I/O.

panels.title: CPU cores used vs GOMAXPROCS
panels.description: CPU cores consumed per instance (user plus system time per second, solid) against its GOMAXPROCS (dashed), the number of cores the Go scheduler will use. When the solid line reaches the dashed one the process is CPU-bound and request latency grows.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open file descriptors per instance (left axis) and their share of the process limit (right axis, dashed). Sockets dominate, so this follows client and origin connections; filesystem and bbolt caches and log files add more. Approaching 100% leads to failed accepts. Empty on platforms where the process collector cannot read descriptor counts.

targets.expr: max by (instance) (process_open_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) / on (instance) (max by (instance) (process_max_fds{job=~"$job", instance=~"$instance"}) > 0)

panels.title: Heap in use and GC goal
panels.description: Per instance: heap bytes in in-use spans (solid) and the heap goal the garbage collector is working to stay under in the current cycle (dashed). In-memory caches live on this heap, so it grows with their contents. Near GOMEMLIMIT the runtime holds the goal down, so it flattens while GC cycles/s rises; the limit itself is drawn against total Go runtime memory in the resident memory panel.

panels.title: Heap allocation rate
panels.description: Bytes (left axis) and objects (right axis, dashed) allocated on the heap per second, per instance. This is the most direct efficiency signal for a proxy cache: allocation drives GC work and tail latency. Compare it with the request rate; allocation per request that grows after an upgrade or config change is a regression worth investigating.

panels.title: Resident memory, Go runtime memory and GOMEMLIMIT
panels.description: Per instance: resident set size of the process (solid), the memory the Go runtime has obtained from the OS minus what it has returned (dashed), and the GOMEMLIMIT soft limit when set (red, dotted). GOMEMLIMIT bounds the Go runtime line, so as that line nears the limit the collector runs far more often. RSS above the Go figure is normal with bbolt or Badger caches (memory-mapped files) and cgo; RSS is what container memory limits and OOM kills act on.

panels.title: GC cycles/s
panels.description: Completed garbage collection cycles per second, per instance. The rate rises with the allocation rate and with heap pressure against GOMEMLIMIT; a jump without a traffic change usually means the live heap grew (for example a memory cache filling up) or the limit is close.

panels.title: GC stop-the-world pauses
panels.description: Longest (solid) and median (dashed) stop-the-world pause among the most recent garbage collections, per instance. Every in-flight request stalls for the pause, so the maximum adds directly to tail latency; healthy Go processes stay well under a millisecond. These are summary quantiles reported by each process and cannot be combined across instances (Prometheus 3 stores the maximum as quantile 1.0, older versions as 1; both are matched).

panels.title: Network I/O (Linux only)
panels.description: Bytes per second received (in, blue) and transmitted (out, green) on the network interfaces of the process's network namespace, per instance. The process collector exports these only on Linux, so this panel is empty on macOS and Windows. In a container this covers the pod's whole network namespace, including sidecars.
